# /accessibility — audit, fix, and re-verify WCAG 2.2 AA, governed

Turns `$ARGUMENTS` — an EQOne **screen**, **route**, or **PR number**, optionally followed by the
`skip-figma` flag — into a **governed WCAG 2.2 AA audit + fix + re-verify** across the frontend
(`eq-nexus-ui` shell, child MFEs `eq-one-saye-mfe` / `eq-one-sip-mfe` / `eq-one-shares-mfe`,
`eq-one-shared`, and `eq-one-design-system` consumers). Unlike `/review` (which runs a11y as **one
read-only lens** among six), this command goes the full distance: `@a11y` audits, the owning worker
**fixes**, `@a11y` **re-verifies**, and `@critic` gates — looping until clean or budget says stop.

Target under audit: **$ARGUMENTS**

This command is the **main thread**: only it launches subagents by delegating via your `agents` list.
**Subagents never launch further subagents.** Every stage is planned, budgeted, and gated by the
governance trio:

- **@supervisor** owns the run — plans the stages, allocates the tool-call/token budget from
  `budget-policy`, enforces the guardrails (`safety-rails`, `path-policy`, `dedup-policy`,
  `cache-policy`), and makes the go/no-go call between stages.
- **@critic** is the strict quality gate — returns `PASS` / `FAIL`. A `FAIL` **blocks the stage** and
  **loops back to the fix stage** until PASS or `@supervisor` calls stop on budget.
- **@decision** resolves every ambiguity (which MFE owns a screen, whether a violation is a
  design-system swap vs a bespoke-markup fix, proceed-design-blind when Figma is unavailable) with a
  defensible, logged rationale.

## Operating model (always on)

- **Console.** Every stage emits the standardised three-part console via the `console-render` skill
  (see `console/CONSOLE-UX.md`): an **Intro card** at the start, **one block per stage**, and a
  **Summary** at the end. Never print ad-hoc output — route it through `console-render`.
- **Budget.** `@supervisor` plans the stages and allocates the tool-call/token budget per
  `budget-policy`. The `budget-check` skill is tallied after every stage; if a stage would breach the
  ceiling, `@supervisor` narrows remaining work (fewer violations per pass) rather than blowing the
  budget.
- **Model ladder.** Each agent runs at its default tier (`model-routing-policy`) — `@a11y` is
  haiku-cheap because WCAG conformance is overwhelmingly rule-based. Escalate exactly **ONE rung**
  only on low self-eval confidence (<0.7) or two `@critic` FAILs (e.g. `@a11y` → sonnet for a
  non-obvious focus-trap/roving-tabindex restructure); escalation is logged and budgeted, never
  auto-downgraded.
- **Cache.** Read-only fetch/scan work (PR diff, repo scans, `figma-context`, `dna-precheck`) is
  served through `cache-lookup` (keyed `skill_id, version, input_hash`, per `cache-policy`). NEVER
  cache the fix edits, the re-verify audit, `self-evaluate`, `@critic` verdicts, tests, or LLM
  completions.
- **Safety/paths.** Honour `safety-rails` (no secrets, no PII echoed into findings or logs) and
  `path-policy` (fixes land only in the correct MFE / `eq-one-shared` / `eq-one-design-system`; never
  touch BFF — a11y is FE-only). Enforces the EQ rails in `guardrails-registry`: UI **must** use
  `eq-one-design-system`, never hand-rolled (`@design-system`), and common code moves to
  `eq-one-shared` via `@shared-curator` (`dedup-policy`).

## Staged flow

### Stage 0 — Plan & budget (Intro card) (`@supervisor`)
`@supervisor` reads `$ARGUMENTS`, detects the target type (screen / route / PR) and the `skip-figma`
flag, plans the stages, allocates the budget per `budget-policy`, seeds the `TodoWrite` ledger (one
item per audited screen/violation), and emits the **Intro card** via `console-render` (target, MFEs in
scope, design link found Y/N, budget ceiling). Opens the per-run **agent-memory** runtime
(`metadata.json`, `scratchpad.md`, `ledger.jsonl`, `handoff/`) under `.eq-sparks/agent-memory/<run-id>/`
per the `memory-schema` runtime layout so the run is auditable and resumable.

### Stage 1 — Resolve target (+ optional design fetch)
Resolve `$ARGUMENTS` to a concrete set of changed/target FE files and the owning MFE(s):
- **PR number** → fetch the diff via `gh pr diff` (Bash), routed through `cache-lookup` on the head
  SHA; map each changed UI path to its MFE/shell/shared owner.
- **route / screen** → `Grep`/`Glob` the FE repos to locate the component tree backing that route or
  screen, served through `cache-lookup`.
If ownership is ambiguous, launch `@decision` for a logged call. **Conditional design fetch:** IFF a
Figma URL is linked to the target (e.g. on the PR or supplied) **AND** `skip-figma` is **absent**, run
the `figma-context` skill (MCP:figma, via `cache-lookup`) to pull the intended frame/contrast/target
sizes — otherwise emit an **AUTO-SKIPPED** note with the reason (`no Figma URL` / `skip-figma flag set`),
and on `auth_required`/`unreachable` let `@decision` log a defensible "proceed design-blind" call.
Route a **handoff envelope** carrying the file list + ownership map + any `figma_context` to `@a11y`.

### Stage 2 — Audit (`@a11y`)
Launch `@a11y` (haiku, read-only) to audit every in-scope screen/component against **WCAG 2.2 AA**:
aria roles/labels, focus order vs DOM order, visible focus, colour contrast, keyboard operability (no
mouse-only handlers), target size (min 24×24), and reflow. Each finding cites a specific success
criterion (e.g. `WCAG 1.4.3`), `file:line`, severity, and a concrete remediation; findings needing a
non-obvious structural fix are marked **escalation candidates**. `@a11y` runs its **single-shot** loop
and **self-ASSESSES** (it is read-only, produces no diff — it does NOT call the diff-based
`self-evaluate`, so an empty diff never reads as FAIL), then emits a PASS/FAIL findings list as a
**handoff envelope** to the fix stage. Read-only scans use `cache-lookup`. Emits a **stage block** of
the findings + self-assessed confidence.

### Stage 3 — Fix (PARALLEL per violation, by owner)
For each violation, the owning worker applies the surgical fix:
- **Design-system violation** (bespoke control that the design system already provides, wrong
  variant, missing accessible component) → `@design-system` (sonnet) swaps hand-rolled markup for the
  real `eq-one-design-system` component (the facade over `eq-one-studio` Storybook), enforcing the
  design-system rail (`guardrails-registry`).
- **General markup / aria / focus / keyboard fix** that no specialist owns → `@codegen` (sonnet).
Independent violations across different files/MFEs run **in PARALLEL** (see **Parallelisation**). Each
build agent runs its **autoresearch loop** (`methodology/autoresearch-loop.md`): `dna-precheck` BEFORE
editing (reuse > extend > create; common accessible wrappers move to `eq-one-shared` via the
`@shared-curator` + `move-to-shared` path, per `dedup-policy`), then `self-evaluate` **LAST** and a
**handoff envelope** before handoff. Emits a **stage block** of the diffs applied.

### Stage 4 — Re-verify (`@a11y`)
Launch `@a11y` again (read-only) to **re-audit the fixed screens** and prove each violation is actually
closed and nothing regressed (e.g. a focus fix did not break tab order elsewhere). Re-audit of unchanged
neighbours uses `cache-lookup`; the changed surfaces are freshly scanned (never cached). `@a11y`
self-ASSESSES and emits an updated PASS/FAIL list as a **handoff envelope**. Emits a **stage block** of
the re-verification result per finding.

### Stage 5 — Critic gate (`@critic`)
Launch `@critic` (opus) to adversarially review the audit + fixes + re-verification against EQ standards
and WCAG 2.2 AA, returning strict **PASS / FAIL** with required changes. A **FAIL BLOCKS** and routes
the envelope **back to Stage 3** for the owning worker to rework (escalate one tier per the ladder after
two FAILs), then re-verify (Stage 4), until PASS or `@supervisor` calls stop on budget. Emits the gate
block.

### Stage 6 — Summary (`@supervisor`)
`@supervisor` makes the final go/no-go, runs `budget-check` one final time, and aggregates **every**
handoff envelope under `handoff/*.json` (in `seq` order) into the **Summary** via `console-render`:
violations found vs fixed vs deferred, fixes by repo (which MFE / `eq-one-shared` /
`eq-one-design-system`), `@decision` rationales, tier escalations, cache hit-rate, and budget spent vs
ceiling. The `agent-memory` ledger is closed for a clean `/resume`.

## Handoff & memory

Stages **compose** by passing a structured **handoff envelope**, never free text:
- **Routing.** Between stages the orchestrator (the main thread) routes the envelope — written and read
  via the `handoff` skill per `methodology/handoff-protocol.md`, stored at
  `.eq-sparks/agent-memory/<run-id>/handoff/<seq>-<from>-to-<to>.json` — from one agent to the next:
  Stage 1's file list + ownership map + any `figma_context` to `@a11y`; `@a11y`'s findings to the fix
  workers; the workers' diffs back to `@a11y` for re-verify; the re-verify result to `@critic`;
  `@critic`'s verdict to `@supervisor`. On a `@critic` FAIL the envelope routes **back** to the owning
  worker (Stage 3) with the required changes in `open_items`.
- **Memory runtime.** At Stage 0 `@supervisor` opens (and through the run updates) the per-run
  agent-memory directory (`metadata.json`, `scratchpad.md`, idempotent `ledger.jsonl`, `handoff/`)
  under `.eq-sparks/agent-memory/<run-id>/` per the `memory-schema` runtime layout, instantiated from
  `shared/memory/templates/`, and moves each violation `pending` → `done`/`blocked`.
- **Loop + self-eval.** `@a11y` runs its **single-shot** loop and self-ASSESSES (read-only, no diff —
  not the diff-based `self-evaluate`); the fix workers (`@design-system`, `@codegen`) run the
  **autoresearch loop** (`methodology/autoresearch-loop.md`) with `dna-precheck` first and
  `self-evaluate` **LAST** before emitting their envelope at loop step 9.
- **Aggregation.** At Stage 6 `@supervisor` reads every `handoff/*.json` in `seq` order and aggregates
  the chain, decisions, artifacts, budget, and any open items into the **Summary** (`console-render`) —
  reconstructed from on-disk record, not recollection.

## Parallelisation

- **Stage 3 fixes run in PARALLEL where independent.** When `@a11y` returns multiple violations across
  **different files/components/MFEs**, the orchestrator launches the owning workers (`@design-system`,
  `@codegen`) **concurrently** in one batch, since the fixes do not touch the same paths. Violations
  that share a file or where one fix depends on another (e.g. a shared wrapper lifted to `eq-one-shared`
  that other components then consume) are **sequenced** by `@supervisor`, not parallelised.
- **Audit, re-verify, and the gate are SEQUENTIAL barriers.** Stage 2 (audit) must complete before any
  fix; Stage 4 (re-verify) is a **barrier** — all parallel Stage 3 fixes must land before `@a11y`
  re-audits; and the **`@critic` gate (Stage 5) is the barrier** that all re-verified fixes converge on
  before the run can advance to Summary. A `@critic` FAIL re-opens the fix fan-out for only the offending
  violations.

## Steps

1. `@supervisor` parses `$ARGUMENTS` (detect screen/route/PR + `skip-figma`), plans stages + budget
   (`budget-policy`), seeds the `TodoWrite` ledger, opens the **agent-memory** runtime
   (`memory-schema`), and emits the **Intro card** (`console-render`).
2. Resolve the target to FE files + owning MFE(s): `gh pr diff` for a PR (via `cache-lookup` on head
   SHA) or `Grep`/`Glob` for a route/screen; launch `@decision` (`Agent`) for any ambiguous ownership.
   IFF a Figma URL is linked and `skip-figma` is absent, run `figma-context` (via `cache-lookup`); else
   emit an AUTO-SKIPPED note. Hand off the file list + ownership map + any `figma_context` to `@a11y`.
3. Launch `@a11y` (`Agent`) to audit against WCAG 2.2 AA; it self-ASSESSES and emits a PASS/FAIL
   findings list. `budget-check` after the stage.
4. Launch the owning fix workers — `@design-system` (design-system swaps, design-system rail) and/or
   `@codegen` (general aria/focus/keyboard fixes) — **in PARALLEL** for independent violations
   (sequence shared files). Each runs `dna-precheck` first and `self-evaluate` last (lift common
   wrappers to `eq-one-shared` via `@shared-curator`/`move-to-shared`, `dedup-policy`).
5. Launch `@a11y` (`Agent`) again to **re-verify** each violation is closed with no regression
   (barrier: all Stage 4 fixes must land first).
6. Launch `@critic` (`Agent`) for the strict PASS/FAIL gate. On FAIL, loop back to step 4 for the
   offending violations (escalate one tier after two FAILs per `model-routing-policy`), then re-verify;
   on PASS, continue.
7. Launch `@supervisor` (`Agent`) for the go/no-go verdict; run final `budget-check`; aggregate every
   `handoff/*.json` envelope in `seq` order; emit the **Summary** (`console-render`) and close the
   `agent-memory` ledger.

## Usage

```
/accessibility 4821
```
Audit PR #4821: fetch its diff, follow any linked Figma design, run the WCAG 2.2 AA audit, fix the
violations, re-verify, and gate with `@critic`.

```
/accessibility /saye/dashboard
```
Audit a route: locate the component tree backing `/saye/dashboard` in the SAYE MFE, then the full
audit → fix → re-verify → gate flow.

```
/accessibility ContributionSummaryPanel
```
Audit a named screen/component wherever it lives across the MFEs; `@decision` resolves ownership if it
appears in more than one place.

```
/accessibility 4821 skip-figma
```
Same PR flow, but Stage 1's Figma fetch is AUTO-SKIPPED (`skip-figma flag set`) — useful when the design
is unchanged or unavailable; the audit proceeds design-blind and `@decision` records the gap.

---

## Resume & checkpoint (interruption-safe)

This orchestrator is resumable after any interruption (IDE closed, crash, cancel). At **Stage 0** the orchestrator writes `.eq-sparks/agent-memory/<run-id>/metadata.json` with `orchestrator: "accessibility"` and the ordered `stages` list, and seeds `ledger.jsonl` with each stage `pending`. After **every** stage passes its gate, the orchestrator — the main thread, which holds `Write`; `@supervisor` is read-only and only specifies *what* to record — **appends a `done` line** to `ledger.jsonl` with that stage's `task_id` + `content_hash` (per [dedup-policy](../shared/guardrails/dedup-policy.md) / [memory-schema](../shared/memory/memory-schema.md)). The ledger is written **incrementally after every stage, not only at the end**, so finished stages survive an interruption. PBI/Figma context is read from the no-TTL **story cache** `.eq-sparks/cache/story-cache/<pbi>.json` and is **never re-fetched**. If interrupted, **`/resume`** reads `metadata.json`, re-enters *this* orchestrator at the first `pending` stage, and skips work already marked `done`.
